subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: What failure-reporting and mitigation boundary should OpenClaw own when cron work is interrupted by Gateway memory pressure or event-loop starvation?
rationale: Current code can mark interrupted runs after restart, but failureAlert still runs inside the same potentially wedged Gateway process, so automation should not choose between memory-only repair, restart-aware accounting, and external alerting without maintainer intent.

options.title: Prove and keep scoped
options.body: Keep #87109 open and require a macOS launchd soak/profile on current main before deciding whether the remaining fix belongs in memory-core, cron, Gateway diagnostics, or supervisor integration.

options.title: Split memory and alert work
options.body: Track root-cause memory plateau work separately from a cron lifecycle design that reports started-but-never-completed jobs after restart or from outside the Gateway process.

options.title: Close after restart accounting proof
options.body: Treat current interrupted-run accounting plus memory watcher fixes as sufficient only if maintainers accept process-local alerts and produce representative soak proof showing the original workload no longer starves.

recommendation.title: Prove and keep scoped
recommendation.body: Keep #87109 open and require a macOS launchd soak/profile on current main before deciding whether the remaining fix belongs in memory-core, cron, Gateway diagnostics, or supervisor integration.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the central memory watcher fix and are the strongest current routing signal for the remaining memory backend and soak-proof decision.
